_doc: Scenes and narration of 'Enforce mode, step by step' (Phase 1). One entry per scene; each language is a list of sentences (cues). Write numbers in words. Then run narrate.py on this folder. The organisation, repository, people and pull requests shown are fictional (acme).

en: Phase one of Graft is built: it can count approvals, watch main, and talk to agents.
But it still starts in report mode, and nothing enforces until an operator says so.
Each repository has three keys: policy mode, guard mode, and M C P write.
The operator sets them with the Graft command line, never in graft dot yaml.
Above them sits a server ceiling, which defaults to report, and the lower of the two wins.
Any GitHub write that the effective mode does not allow is refused.
In report mode, the policy check stays neutral, and says what enforce mode would conclude.
In enforce mode, Graft counts real approvals: write access, on the current head, from verified team members.
A new push makes earlier approvals stale.
The check turns green only when the policy is met.
When something must merge now, a maintainer adds the break-glass label.
The check passes for that one commit, and the next push needs the label again.
A label from someone with triage rights is ignored.
Every bypass is written to the audit log.
After a merge, the guard watches the checks on main.
When a check goes red, it waits for the next commit to confirm the failure, so a flaky test is not blamed.
Then it names the culprit, in a comment on the pull request that broke main.
In enforce mode, the guard opens a revert pull request.
It builds the revert from file versions alone, without reading any code.
If a later commit touched the same files, it stops, and asks a human.
Auto-merge is opt-in for trivial and logic reverts, never for sensitive ones, and branch protection still decides.
Agents can talk to Graft directly, through an M C P server with four tools.
Each token is scoped to one repository, and stored only as a hash.
Provenance an agent reports can tighten a verdict, never loosen it.
Open change can open a pull request, only when M C P write is on, and only signed commits let approvals count.
A runbook takes each pilot repository through the stages, one at a time.
Install in report mode, watch for two weeks, then enforce the policy, then the guard.
The Phase one gate measures four things, across five pilots.
Thirty percent of pull requests merged with no human, half the review minutes, eighty percent of breakages caught, and no rise in escaped defects.
Report first, then enforce one repository at a time.
Every step, and its rollback, is in the docs.
